harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Published the staged public and staff trees on node1 TCP port 8080. Public content is anonymous; staff content requires HTTP Basic authentication as reader. The service survives node restart, runs unprivileged, and preserves the legacy OS, kernel, and supplied files.
actions_performed: Installed a Python 2.5-compatible HTTP service using the existing runtime.
Protected /staff/ and all staff files with HTTP Basic authentication.
Disabled directory listings and restricted serving to the public and staff trees.
Rebooted node1 and verified automatic recovery.

evidence.requirement: Public content is anonymously available on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: Before and after reboot, the service listened on 0.0.0.0:8080 and /public/ returned HTTP 200 with an exact match to the staged index.

evidence.requirement: Staff content requires reader Basic authentication
evidence.summary: Anonymous and incorrect-password requests returned 401 without exposing staff content; valid reader credentials returned exact copies of the staged staff index and roster.

evidence.requirement: Password file and directory listings are not served
evidence.summary: Direct and encoded-traversal requests for access.txt returned 404; /public/ served its index with no directory-listing markers.

evidence.requirement: Supplied pages remain intact and the legacy platform is retained
evidence.summary: The four supplied files retained their paths, sizes, ownership, and permissions; served pages matched their staged sources. Kernel remained 2.6.22-14-generic.

evidence.requirement: Service starts automatically and runs with reduced privilege
evidence.summary: SysV startup links were installed; after reboot the service returned automatically and ran as nobody.

Healthy baseline boot ID 7954dab4-7c96-41fa-a1b7-63a2f6aa4e29 was captured, reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed to a5c705b9-ea61-4531-93a7-3d072f3768ea, and full service, authentication, content, and data recovery were verified.
